featured.title: Trump's UN Diplomacy Comes as Iran, Ukraine and Energy Security Take Centre Stage
featured.content: US President Donald Trump is conducting a wide-ranging diplomatic programme around the UN General Assembly as wars, energy disruption and technology competition dominate discussions in New York. US–Iran communication remains possible, but major differences over military pressure, sanctions and the Strait of Hormuz continue. Ukraine is also seeking US support for an energy-focused truce with Russia, while European governments are dealing with the economic consequences of elevated energy prices.
featured.imageQuery: Donald Trump United Nations General Assembly 2026

articles.title: US–Iran Diplomacy Continues as Hormuz Remains a Global Energy Risk
articles.content: US President Donald Trump has said communication with Iran is continuing while also warning that further military action remains possible if an agreement cannot be reached. Iran has separately indicated that it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within about a week if US military pressure and the blockade on Iranian ports are eased. Iranian officials say their delegation in New York has authority to pursue diplomacy. The situation remains fluid, with no confirmed comprehensive settlement.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz oil tanker shipping Middle East

articles.title: Hormuz Vessel Traffic Falls to Extremely Low Levels
articles.content: Preliminary shipping data indicated that only two commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, compared with a pre-conflict average of roughly 125 large commercial vessels a day. The data may not capture vessels operating with tracking systems switched off. Two vessels were also reported hit by projectiles while transiting the area, although responsibility for those incidents had not been established.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz tanker shipping satellite

articles.title: Ukraine Seeks Energy Truce as Zelenskyy Meets Trump
articles.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is seeking US support for an agreement to halt attacks on energy infrastructure as he engages with President Trump during the UN meetings. Russia and Ukraine have continued aerial attacks affecting energy and critical infrastructure. Kyiv is particularly focused on protecting its energy system ahead of winter. There is currently no confirmed new energy ceasefire.
articles.imageQuery: Volodymyr Zelenskyy United Nations New York 2026

articles.title: Germany Raises 2026 and 2027 Growth Forecasts
articles.content: Germany's leading economic research institutes have raised their joint forecast for economic growth to 1.3% in 2026, up from an earlier estimate of 0.6%, and to 1.1% in 2027 from 0.9%. The revision follows stronger-than-expected economic performance during the first half of the year. The institutes nevertheless expect only 0.4% growth in 2028, highlighting continuing structural challenges.

articles.title: France Faces Weak Growth and Rising Energy Pressure
articles.content: France's economic outlook remains under pressure. INSEE expects the French economy to grow by 0.4% in 2026, while the government has lowered its own forecast to 0.5%. The slowdown reflects weaker purchasing power, subdued investment, higher energy costs and wider economic uncertainty. The government has also expanded targeted fuel assistance as households and businesses face higher energy costs.

articles.title: Nigeria Approves 830,000 Tonnes of Petrol Imports for Q4
articles.content: Nigeria's downstream petroleum regulator has approved import permits covering 830,000 metric tonnes of petrol for the fourth quarter of 2026. The permits were issued to six major marketers. The decision comes despite the expansion of domestic refining, including Dangote Refinery, and means imported petrol will remain part of Nigeria's supply mix during the final quarter of the year. The regulator and industry participants continue to balance domestic production, imports and seasonal demand.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria petrol station fuel supply Lagos

articles.title: Dangote IPO Keeps Nigeria's Capital Market in Focus
articles.content: The proposed Dangote Refinery IPO continues to attract major attention among Nigerian investors. The offer is priced at ₦525 per share and aims to raise around $1.6 billion. Supporters see the listing as an opportunity to deepen domestic participation in the capital market, while financial commentators continue to stress that shares carry investment risk and that investors should assess valuation, liquidity and market conditions rather than assume guaranteed returns.

articles.title: Typhoon Dujuan Leaves Deaths and Power Outages in Japan
articles.content: Typhoon Dujuan brought torrential rain, flooding and landslides to parts of Japan's Pacific coast. At least four people have died and several others were reported missing as emergency crews continued search operations. Around 45,000 households were affected by power outages. The storm was moving northeast away from Japan, while authorities continued monitoring flood and landslide risks.

articles.title: DeepSeek Joins UN Discussions on Artificial Intelligence Security
articles.content: Chinese AI company DeepSeek is among the technology companies participating in discussions around artificial intelligence risks at the United Nations. The discussions come as Washington and Beijing continue competing over advanced AI, chips and technology supply chains while also exploring ways to manage the security risks associated with increasingly powerful AI systems.
articles.imageQuery: artificial intelligence technology server data centre

articles.title: US–China AI Competition Remains a Global Economic Issue
articles.content: Artificial intelligence remains central to the wider US–China relationship. Both countries are developing domestic AI ecosystems while competing over advanced semiconductors, computing infrastructure, investment and technology standards. The issue is also becoming part of international discussions over AI safety and governance, particularly as world leaders gather at the UN.
articles.imageQuery: US China artificial intelligence technology chips

articles.title: Asian Games Continue in Aichi-Nagoya
articles.content: The 2026 Asian Games continue in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with athletes from across Asia competing in dozens of sports. India's campaign includes shooting, weightlifting, badminton and fencing, while competitors from China, Japan, South Korea and other nations continue pursuing medals. The Games run from September 19 to October 4.

articles.title: Oil Markets Remain Highly Sensitive to Middle East Diplomacy
articles.content: Oil prices remain volatile as traders assess US–Iran diplomacy, the security of the Strait of Hormuz and the recovery of Saudi export infrastructure. Brent crude has recently traded around the $100-a-barrel level. Saudi Arabia has resumed operations on its East-West pipeline, while shipping through Hormuz remains far below normal levels. Any sustained disruption could continue affecting fuel prices, transport costs and inflation worldwide.

articles.title: US Markets Watch Oil, AI and Federal Reserve Signals
articles.content: US financial markets remain influenced by developments in the Middle East, artificial intelligence and interest-rate expectations. Technology stocks have benefited from renewed enthusiasm around AI, while higher energy prices continue to create inflation concerns. Federal Reserve officials have indicated that inflation risks remain important as policymakers assess the path of interest rates.

morningSummary: Good morning and welcome to RadiantWaves Media. World leaders are gathering in New York as the UN General Assembly continues against the backdrop of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, energy-market disruption and rapid advances in artificial intelligence. US–Iran diplomacy remains uncertain, Ukraine is seeking an energy truce, Europe is assessing the economic consequences of higher energy costs, Nigeria is balancing domestic refining with additional petrol imports, and Japan is recovering from Typhoon Dujuan.
bigQuestion: As wars, energy prices and technology reshape the global economy, how can countries protect their citizens while keeping international cooperation alive?
quoteOfTheDay: A world that changes quickly demands more than quick reactions; it demands the patience to understand, the courage to question and the wisdom to act.
